facts.raw_span: an erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 45 mm/h
an erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 45 mm/h

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of polyarthritis, joint swelling, and high antinuclear antibody titer, along with the presence of anti-centromere antibodies, are consistent with Systemic Sclerosis.

The patient's symptoms of polyarthritis, joint swelling, and high antinuclear antibody titer, along with the presence of anti-centromere antibodies and Raynaud's phenomenon, are consistent with Limited Systemic Sclerosis.
The patient's symptoms of progressive dyspnea, orthopnea, and high pulmonary arterial systolic pressure are consistent with Idiopathic Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.

The patient's symptoms of polyarthritis, joint swelling, and high antinuclear antibody titer, along with the presence of anti-centromere antibodies, are consistent with Mixed Connective Tissue Disease.
The patient's symptoms of polyarthritis and joint swelling are consistent with Rheumatoid Arthritis, although the negative rheumatoid factor test result makes this diagnosis less likely.

The patient's high antinuclear antibody titer and presence of anti-centromere antibodies are consistent with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus, although the lack of other typical SLE symptoms makes this diagnosis less likely.
The patient's symptoms of progressive dyspnea, orthopnea, and high pulmonary arterial systolic pressure are consistent with Pulmonary Vasculitis.

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of progressive dyspnea, orthopnea, and high pulmonary arterial systolic pressure, along with the presence of anti-centromere antibodies and high antinuclear antibody titer, are consistent with Connective Tissue Disease-associated Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.

The patient's symptoms of polyarthritis, joint swelling, and high antinuclear antibody titer, along with the presence of anti-centromere antibodies, are consistent with Undifferentiated Connective Tissue Disease.
The patient's symptoms of polyarthritis, joint swelling, and high antinuclear antibody titer, along with the presence of anti-centromere antibodies, are consistent with Overlap Syndrome.

rationales.F03: Polyarthritis is a common feature of several connective tissue diseases, including Systemic Sclerosis, Limited Systemic Sclerosis, Mixed Connective Tissue Disease, and Rheumatoid Arthritis.
rationales.F04: Joint swelling is a common feature of several connective tissue diseases, including Systemic Sclerosis, Limited Systemic Sclerosis, Mixed Connective Tissue Disease, and Rheumatoid Arthritis.
rationales.F05: A 3-year history of progressive dyspnea is suggestive of Idiopathic Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension or Connective Tissue Disease-associated Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
rationales.F06: NYHA class IV indicates severe pulmonary hypertension, which is consistent with Idiopathic Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension or Connective Tissue Disease-associated Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
rationales.F10: A PASP of 80 mm Hg is indicative of pulmonary hypertension, which is consistent with Idiopathic Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension or Connective Tissue Disease-associated Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
rationales.F12: An antinuclear antibody titer of 1:320 is suggestive of an autoimmune disorder, such as Systemic Sclerosis, Limited Systemic Sclerosis, or Mixed Connective Tissue Disease.
